sections.html:
Little Rock is Arkansas's capital, its most populous city and the Pulaski County seat. It had 202,591 residents in the 2020 census, and the 2025 estimate is 206,427. North Little Rock lies across the Arkansas River as a separate city.

Neighborhoods range widely: Hillcrest, The Heights, Quapaw Quarter, Downtown, South End, West End, Southwest Little Rock, Chenal Valley and Pulaski Heights. An older central house and a newer western subdivision face different buyers, different upkeep and different storm exposure, so price and describe yours by its own neighborhood.

Hospitals, banks, transport and retail carry the local economy. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences employs more than 10,552 people and the city government more than 2,500. Colleges add renters and buyers: the University of Arkansas at Little Rock, Philander Smith College, Arkansas Baptist College and Pulaski Technical College are all in or near the city. A job transfer or a hospital contract ending can push an owner to sell sooner than planned.

Because the metro is spread across river, creek and hill terrain, buyers also ask about drainage and which side of town the house sits on. Be ready to answer where water goes after a hard rain.

July highs run near 91.7 degrees, humidity stays high, and about 50.42 inches of precipitation fall each year. Heat and moisture are hard on roofs, HVAC systems and crawl spaces, and buyers' inspectors check all three.

Tornadoes are the sharper risk. On March 31, 2023, an EF3 tornado with 165 mph winds started in the Martindale area and moved northeast through Chenal Valley, Breckenridge, Cammack Village and Burns Park. A city count listed 2,648 structures damaged or destroyed, and 588 properties took major damage. Insurance claims paid in Little Rock passed $489 million by the end of 2023, a figure that includes other severe weather that day.

If your house was hit, collect the claim letters, repair invoices and permits in one folder before you list.

Most of the city is in the Little Rock School District, whose five public high schools are Central, Southwest, West, Hall STEAM Magnet and Parkview Arts and Science Magnet. Know the attendance zone for your address before you talk price with a buyer.

Seven interstate routes serve the area: I-40, I-30, I-57 (partly unbuilt), I-430, I-440, I-630 and I-530. Clinton National Airport is reached from I-440. Rock Region Metro runs the buses, and the Metro Streetcar covers 3.4 miles with 14 stops.

The Code Enforcement Division handles overgrown lots, trash, illegal dumping, non-running vehicles, graffiti, unsecured vacant houses, dilapidated structures and minimum housing code violations. Residents report problems through a Neighborhood Resource Center or by calling 3-1-1. A residential structure that Code Enforcement declares unsafe goes to the Board of Directors for condemnation, and then the city contracts for demolition.

  • Code Enforcement Division: 500 West Markham Street, Room 120, (501) 379-1516.
  • Complaint line: 3-1-1.
  • An unsecured or fire-damaged house can be condemned, which makes a conventional sale much harder.

Call before you sign anything if you suspect an open violation on your house, and ask what is on file.

Little Rock has 27 National Register historic districts, but that listing is honorary and puts no restrictions on private owners. Only the MacArthur Park Local Historic District requires a Certificate of Appropriateness before exterior work, site design changes or demolition. The Capitol Zoning District has its own rules for property near the Capitol. Selling a house, as opposed to altering it, does not need a certificate.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Pulaski County
sections.html:
Recording detailRequirement
WhereReal Estate Department, Pulaski Circuit and County Clerk, Room 102, 401 West Markham Street
HoursMonday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Fee$15 first page, $5 each additional page
DocumentsOriginal signatures, grantor and grantee, Prepared By statement, Transfer of Tax form, notarization
Photo IDRequired under Act 752, except for attorneys, brokers, financial institution representatives and government representatives

The office takes filings in person, by mail or through approved e-recording vendors. If you file electronically, use an approved vendor.

sections.h2: Property tax and the transfer tax
sections.html: Property tax is collected starting the first business day of March and runs through October 15 of the following year. After that date a 10 percent penalty applies. Act 139 of 2023 puts reappraisals on a four-year cycle, a homestead's taxable value can climb 5 percent a year, and anyone appealing to the county board of equalization must schedule it by the third Monday in August. On top of that comes the state transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes or a condemnation notice
sections.html:
Two problems slow Little Rock sales more than any others: unpaid tax and open city violations. Tax comes out of your proceeds at closing, and the penalty keeps adding up after October 15, so a payoff figure from the county is worth getting while you compare offers. A condemnation or demolition notice is harder, because a buyer who needs a loan usually cannot close on a house the city has declared unsafe.

Owners in that spot often choose a cash buyer who accepts the house as it is. Whatever you choose, tell every buyer about an open notice at the start. A title search will find it anyway, and surprises late in the process cost you the most.

After you accept an offer, the title company confirms who owns the house, searches for liens and prepares the settlement statement. The statement lists the mortgage payoff, the tax split, any amount owed to the city and the transfer tax. Everyone who holds title must sign the deed in front of a notary, and then the Real Estate Department records it. A buyer using a loan adds an appraisal and lender conditions, which stretch the schedule. A buyer paying cash does not.

You can list through an agent, sell the house yourself or take a cash offer. The city has a wide range of homes, so a renovated house in Hillcrest and a dated rental in the southwest may take completely different routes.

  • House with code violations: ask the city what is open before you sign anything.
  • Storm damage: an as-is sale avoids a repair bid.
  • Inherited property: confirm who has authority to sign.
  • Rental with tenants: a buyer may take the property subject to the lease.

A cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal and repair demands, so the closing mostly depends on how fast the title company clears ownership and liens. Gather the deed, your latest tax statement and a mortgage payoff figure before you ask for offers.

faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 206,427 residents, after the 2020 census counted 202,591.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell a house in Little Rock?
faqs.a: No. Only owners in the MacArthur Park Local Historic District need a Certificate of Appropriateness, and only before exterior work, site changes or demolition.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a Little Rock house?
faqs.a: At the Pulaski Circuit and County Clerk's Real Estate Department, 401 West Markham Street, Room 102. The fee is $15 for the first page and $5 for each extra page.

faqs.q: What happens if my Little Rock house is condemned?
faqs.a: After Code Enforcement declares a residential structure unsafe, it goes to the city's Board of Directors for condemnation, and the city can contract for demolition. Call (501) 379-1516 to learn what applies to your property.

faqs.q: When are Pulaski County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By October 15 of the year after assessment. A 10 percent penalty applies to unpaid tax after that date.
